same_basis_candidates.why_it_applies: Nearer read-across analog than milk powder: GB 2762-2025 Table 7 item 3.1 'Beans (dried pulses and flours milled from dried pulses)' is a dry-as-sold plant food, matching dried seaweed on both product origin (plant) and basis (dry, product as placed on market); in force 2026-09-02.
Same instrument, Table 7 item 1.1 'Cereals': a second dry-as-sold plant staple at 1.0 mg/kg total Cr, concurring with the dried-pulse line as the nearest dry plant-food analog.
Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 7 'Pulses' at 1 mg/kg total Cr, solid food recorded as-sold; concurring second sovereign for dry plant foods.
Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2 item 7 'Cereals' at 1 mg/kg total Cr, as-sold; concurring second sovereign for dry plant foods.

cells.reason: The anchor's scope 'Milk powder and modified milk powder (GB 2762-2025 Table 7, item 6.2)' does not cover seaweed, and the read-across is not the nearest same-basis sovereign instrument: the same Table 7 carries dry-as-sold plant-food lines (beans/dried pulses item 3.1 and cereals item 1.1, both 1.0 mg/kg total Cr) that match dried nori/wakame/kombu/dulse on plant origin and dry basis, whereas milk powder matches on dryness only; Hong Kong Cap 132V pulses and cereals concur at 1 mg/kg. GB 2762-2025 sets no chromium line for its Annex A algae category and clause 3.5 restricts fresh-to-dried conversion to dried aquatic products and dried edible fungi, so no direct sovereign Cr ML exists for dried seaweed and the nearest dry plant-food analog at 1000 should bind. The fresh-vegetable rows (GB Table 7 item 2.1 and HK 'Vegetables, other than pulses', both 500) are fresh-weight lines that would scale up under HK regulation 3(2)(b) for dried product, and the HK schedule names 'Seaweed' as its own item where it means to cover it, so they are not taken at face value on this dry cell.
